newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Vitatron to move production abroad.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Vitatron to move production abroad.

text.p: Vitatron, a Dutch subsidiary of Medtronic Inc of the U.S. specialising in pacemaker research and development (R&D), said on Wednesday it planned to strengthen its R&D and marketing departments and move part of its production abroad over the next one or two years.
The changes are part of a two-year restructuring programme, Vitatron said in a statement.

The main part of Vitatron's annual 20,000 to 25,000 pacemaker production now in Dieren will move to Lausanne in Switzerland and the rest to Puerto Rico, Vitatron's general director Jan Dil told Reuters.
Both sites currently have production facilities of some 100,000 pacemakers a year, he said.
Some 130 Dutch jobs of 500 worldwide might be involved, the company said, adding it would assist employees to find work.
"The reason behind this restructuring is the necessity to heavily invest in R&D and marketing for new, advanced pacemaker systems over the next couple of years," Vitatron said.
Vitatron said the transfer of pacemaker production to the automatised mass production lines of its parent company in Puerto Rico and Switzerland and was necessary to enable the investments needed.
It also pointed to increased worldwide pressure on health care budgets.
The company said it expected the higher investments in R&D and marketing to lead to growth of its activities and employment.
